title: Research on a Cow Rumination Behavior Recognition Method by Integrating Biformer and GSConv
content: Cow rumination behavior monitoring is crucial in the precision management of dairy farming as this behavior serves as a key indicator for assessing cow health and productivity. However, noncontact, video-based cow rumination behavior monitoring encounters challenges, such as varying shooting angles, random distributions of individual cows, and complex outdoor environments; hence, accurately identifying changes in the mouth region during cow rumination is particularly challenging. In this study, based on real farming environment data, we constructed a multienvironment cow rumination dataset and proposed a Biformer–YOLOv7 model, which combines double-routing attention (Biformer) and lightweight convolution (GSConv) techniques to effectively recognize a small target region around a cow’s mouth. We compared the performance of YOLOv3, YOLOv4, YOLOv5, YOLOv7, and the proposed Biformer–YOLOv7 model for cow mouth region detection. Results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms others in terms of mean average precision, recall rate, detection accuracy, and detection speed. Specifically, the average precision of cow mouth region detection reaches 95.90%, the recall rate is 91.16%, accuracy achieves 93.73%, and the detection speed reaches 35.6 FPS, meeting real-time requirements. Moreover, the proposed model demonstrates high accuracy in recognizing and locating cows even under partial occlusion, overcast, and nighttime conditions, exhibiting robustness and applicability. Furthermore, compared with the manual recognition of the rumination behavior, average error in the rumination frames and chewing counts are 4.2% and 3.09%, respectively, indicating the wide application prospects of the Biformer–YOLOv7 model for cow farming video monitoring and management.
